comparisons.peer_topic: Highly competitive and evolving market conditions
comparisons.peer_summary: The markets in which AMD's products are sold are highly competitive and rapidly evolving, with intense competition expected due to rapid technological changes, new industry standards, and frequent introductions of competitive products by current or new competitors, including those who may adapt more quickly to emerging technologies.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose that their respective industries are highly competitive and characterized by rapid technological changes, evolving standards, and aggressive pricing. AVGO specifically notes that competitors often have longer operating histories, greater resources, or government support, while AMD emphasizes the risk of new competitors adapting more quickly to emerging technologies.

sentences.text: The industries in which we operate are highly competitive and characterized by rapid technological changes, evolving industry standards, changes in customer requirements, often aggressive pricing practices and, in some cases, new delivery methods.

Some of our competitors have longer operating histories, greater name recognition or presence in key markets, a larger installed customer base, larger technical staff, a more comprehensive IP portfolio or better patent protection, more established relationships with vendors or suppliers, or greater manufacturing, distribution, financial, research and development, technical and marketing resources than us.
The markets in which our products are sold are highly competitive and rapidly evolving.

We expect that competition will continue to be intense due to rapid technological changes, new and evolving industry standards, changing customer preferences and requirements, and frequent introductions by our competitors or new competitors of products that may provide better performance/experience or that may include additional features that render our products comparatively less competitive.
In addition, we are entering markets with current and new competitors who may be able to adapt more quickly to customer requirements and emerging technologies.

comparisons.peer_topic: New Market Competition and Investment Returns
comparisons.peer_summary: New businesses in AI, cloud-to-edge, and other areas introduce new competition and require significant investment with no guarantee of adequate returns. Failures in AI products or the foundry business could lead to asset impairments, restructuring charges, and opportunity costs.
comparisons.comparison: While AVGO focuses on the structural advantages of existing competitors (resources, history, government support), INTC focuses on the risks introduced by *new* sources of competition in developing areas like AI and foundry services. Both disclose that these new or existing competitors may have well-developed technologies, ecosystems, customer bases, and lower prices or costs, creating a challenging competitive landscape.

sentences.text: Some of our competitors have longer operating histories, greater name recognition or presence in key markets, a larger installed customer base, larger technical staff, a more comprehensive IP portfolio or better patent protection, more established relationships with vendors or suppliers, or greater manufacturing, distribution, financial, research and development, technical and marketing resources than us.

We face competition from companies that receive financial and other support from their home country government, customers who develop competing products, public cloud providers, numerous smaller companies that specialize in specific aspects of the highly fragmented software industry, open source authors who provide software and IP for free, and competitors who offer their products through try-and-buy or freemium models.

These new and developing areas and products represent a significant portion of our revenue growth opportunity, and they also introduce new sources of competition in not just new and evolving markets but also in our existing markets.

These new sources of competition can include established competitors with well-developed and highly competitive technologies, ecosystems, and customer bases, lower prices, margins, or costs, and greater brand recognition.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces intense competition from major players like Samsung and SK hynix, who may use aggressive pricing, have greater resources, or benefit from industry consolidation, potentially putting the company at a disadvantage.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU highlight the risk of aggressive pricing practices by competitors seeking to gain market share. Additionally, both note that some competitors are larger conglomerates with greater resources to invest in technology and withstand market downturns, and both explicitly mention industry consolidation as a factor that could disadvantage them.

comparisons.peer_topic: Competitive risks impacting market share and financial results
comparisons.peer_summary: Intensifying competition from rivals with cheaper or better products, longer operating histories, and greater resources, as well as from customers developing in-house solutions, may reduce demand for NVIDIA's products and harm its ability to establish meaningful revenue.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both identify that competitors may possess longer operating histories, more comprehensive intellectual property portfolios, and greater financial, sales, and marketing resources. Both companies warn that these advantages could allow competitors to acquire market share more effectively or prevent the company from doing so.

sentences.text: Some of our competitors have longer operating histories, greater name recognition or presence in key markets, a larger installed customer base, larger technical staff, a more comprehensive IP portfolio or better patent protection, more established relationships with vendors or suppliers, or greater manufacturing, distribution, financial, research and development, technical and marketing resources than us.

Some of our competitors operate their own fabrication facilities, and have longer operating histories, larger customer bases, more comprehensive IP portfolios and patent protections, more design wins, and greater financial, sales, marketing and distribution resources than we do.

These competitors may be able to acquire market share and/or prevent us from doing so, more effectively identify and capitalize upon opportunities in new markets and end-user trends, more quickly transition their products, and impinge on our ability to procure sufficient foundry capacity and scarce input materials during a supply-constrained environment, which could harm our business.

comparisons.peer_summary: Competition may intensify as competitors expand offerings, reduce prices, or enter the industry, driven by factors like OEM concentrations, vertical integration, government intervention, and the demand for AI capabilities.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and QCOM both identify government intervention or support as a specific competitive factor, noting that some competitors receive financial or other support from their home countries. Both also describe an environment of intense competition where competitors may reduce prices to maintain or attract customers.

sentences.text: We face competition from companies that receive financial and other support from their home country government, customers who develop competing products, public cloud providers, numerous smaller companies that specialize in specific aspects of the highly fragmented software industry, open source authors who provide software and IP for free, and competitors who offer their products through try-and-buy or freemium models.

The industries in which we operate are highly competitive and characterized by rapid technological changes, evolving industry standards, changes in customer requirements, often aggressive pricing practices and, in some cases, new delivery methods.

Competition may intensify as our current competitors expand their product offerings, improve their products or reduce the prices of their products as part of a strategy to maintain existing business and customers or attract new business and customers, as new opportunities develop, and as new competitors enter the industry.

Competition in the semiconductor industry is affected by various factors that include, among others: OEM concentrations; vertical integration; competition in certain geographic regions; government intervention or support of national industries or competitors; the ability to maintain product differentiation in light of evolving industry standards and speed of technological change (including the transition to smaller geometry process technologies, the demand for always on, always connected capabilities, the increasing use of AI and machine learning technologies and the need to run complex AI-based applications on devices); access to capacity in the supply chain; and value-added features that drive selling prices and consumer demand for new devices.
